texts.li: [lowtech,winter] Stuck fast on the frozen track below the colony, with a cracked axle and a long night coming, a {FACTION} caravan has sent someone up to ask for help. {A_nameDef} has the best hands for it. If the colony would rather not send anyone, they'll pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE} and fix it themselves.

[!lowtech,summer] A {FACTION} trade truck has boiled over and thrown a part on the road outside the colony, and its drivers are sitting in the shade of it, arguing. They'd welcome {A_nameDef}'s help, or they'll pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE}.

[colony:Open] Merchants of {FACTION} have broken down on the road, and say they came this way because they'd heard the colony helps travelers. They'd welcome {A_nameDef}, the best hands the colony has, or will pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE} to mend it themselves.

[spring] {FACTION} came out of the winter with empty stores and a whole spring still to get through. They want {TALE} from the colony, for {COUNT} silver, more than a trader would pay.\n\nThey'll send for it in five days, all of it or none.

[colony:Hardworking] A colony that works as hard as this one must have plenty, {FACTION} reckon, and they've sent an order on the strength of it: {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver, well above a trader's price.\n\nTheir people come for it in five days, and it's the whole order or none.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a tinker of {FACTION}, has come in from the cold with frost on {X_possessive} collar and a cart of tools. Winter is mending season, {X_nameDef} says, and for {COUNT} silver every worn coat and dull blade in the colony will be good as new by morning.

[skill:Crafting] {X_nameDef}, a tinker of {FACTION}, set up {X_possessive} cart in the yard, and {A_nameDef} has been looking over {X_possessive} tools ever since. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will mend every worn coat and battered weapon the colony has, and doesn't mind being watched.
[summer] A summer fever came into {FACTION}'s settlement with the flies, and their medicine is gone. They ask the colony for {TALE}, and can pay {COUNT} silver for it if they must.

[colony:Merciful] A runner of {FACTION} came to the gate sure the colony would help, and said so before saying anything else. A fever is going through their settlement, and they've run out of medicine. They ask for {TALE}, and offer {COUNT} silver if the colony wants it.

[water,summer] It's a dry summer, and the spring in the hills between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} is the only water for a day's walk. Both say it's theirs. Both have sent someone to the colony to argue it, and both expect to win.

[herd,lowtech] A bull of {ENEMY}'s broke through a fence and sired half of {FACTION}'s spring calves. {ENEMY} want a share of the calves. {FACTION} want the fence paid for. They've asked the colony to judge.
[land,spring] Planting season has come, and {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have both put stakes in the same strip of bottomland. They've asked the colony to say whose stakes stay in the ground.
[salvage] A wagon of {ENEMY}'s went over in a ditch on {FACTION}'s land, and {FACTION} say whatever lands on their ground is theirs. {ENEMY} disagree, loudly. Both have asked the colony to settle it.
[skill:Plants] {A_nameDef} has been out in the fields at dawn every day this week, just to look. The weather has been perfect for growing, and the open fields are days ahead of where they should be.
[fall] A run of warm, wet days this late in the year has given the crops still in the open fields a last push. {A_nameDef} thinks they'll come in early.
[winter] In the middle of winter, the wind has turned to the south and the snow is going soft. It won't last, but it should stay mild for several days.
[fall] The leaves are down, but the air has gone warm again, as if summer had forgotten something. It should stay mild for several days, and the late crops will have a little longer.

[medieval] {A_nameDef} turned up an old grave, a body laid in a stone-lined pit with a rusted sword across its chest and a few coins in its hands. Someone buried a fighter here, with honors, long before the colony came.
[industrial] Digging out by the old road, {A_nameDef} found a grave no one had marked, with the bones still wrapped in a canvas sheet and a tin box of belongings at their feet.
[winter] Clearing a frozen ditch, {A_nameDef} broke through into an old grave. The cold had kept everything: bones, a bundle of belongings, and a scrap of cloth with a name too faded to read.

lines.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} dug the new grave alone, carefully, and put the dead person's things back beside them before the stone went on.
[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} sorted through the grave goods before the bones were even back in the ground, and kept the best piece. Some of the others won't eat with {A_objective} tonight.

texts.li: [farming] {A_nameDef}'s hoe struck a box buried at the end of a row. Inside, wrapped in waxed cloth, are letters, years of them, between two people a long way apart. The names are from {FACTION}'s lands.

[winter] {A_nameDef} found a box frozen into the bank of the stream and thawed it out by the stove. It's full of old letters between two people, years of them, from a town in {FACTION}'s lands. One is signed only with a drawing of a bird.

lines.li: [winter] {A_nameDef} read the letters by the stove, one bundle after another. By the last of them, most of the colony was sitting up to hear how it ended.

texts.li: [winter] Two young people of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} and {TALE}, came to the gate at dusk, half frozen, sharing one coat. Their families forbade the match, so they ran in the middle of winter. They ask to be taken in.

[colony:Open] {X_nameDef} and {TALE} of {FACTION} heard the colony takes people in, and ran away together on the strength of it. Their families won't have the match. {A_nameDef} found them at the gate with everything they own in one sack.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, has come through the snow from {FACTION}'s lands with a sack of things from home and frost on {X_possessive} eyebrows. {X_nameDef} will stay the night and head back tomorrow.

[summer] {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, {X_nameDef}, has walked in from {FACTION}'s lands with summer fruit from the family's trees. {X_nameDef} will stay the day, and has a long list of questions from the rest of the family.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a fortune teller of {FACTION}, has come in from the cold with a deck of cards wrapped in silk. Winter nights are long, {X_nameDef} says, and for {COUNT} silver every colonist can hear what spring holds.

[colony:Traditional] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} reads fortunes the old way, with bones and ash, and has heard the colony keeps to the old ways. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will read every colonist's fortune tonight.
